Compare Candidate Stratifications Using Oracle Variance Decomposition

Source: R/strata_eval_functions.R
compare_decomposition_oracle.Rd

For each candidate stratification, computes the BS (between-strata) and WS (within-strata) variance components from Theorem 3.2, which together determine the variance reduction from stratified sampling. Returns a summary table and visualization comparing candidates based on oracle information (true residuals).

compare_decomposition_oracle(data, candidates, n_code, Z = "Z")

Arguments

data

Data frame containing Yobs, Yhat, and optionally a treatment indicator column.

candidates

Named list of candidate stratification vectors. Each element should be a factor or character vector of the same length as nrow(data) containing stratum assignments.

n_code

Total number of units to sample for human coding. Required for computing the exact Theorem 3.2 formulas.

Z

Character string specifying the name of the treatment indicator column, or NULL to ignore treatment groups. Default is "Z".

Value

A list with three elements:

summary

Data frame with one row per stratification containing:

  • stratification: Name of the stratification

  • n_strata: Number of strata

  • BS: Between-strata variance component

  • WS: Within-strata variance component

  • BS_minus_WS: Variance reduction (BS - WS)

  • var_ratio: Ratio of max to min within-stratum variance

  • rank: Rank by BS_minus_WS (1 = best)

decomposition_details

List of full decomposition results for each stratification (output from compute_variance_decomposition).

Details

This function uses oracle information (the true residuals Yobs - Yhat) to compute the exact variance decomposition for each candidate stratification. The key metric is BS - WS, which represents the variance reduction achieved by stratified sampling compared to simple random sampling (Theorem 3.2):

$$Var(\hat{\tau}_{SRS}) - Var(\hat{\tau}_{strat}) = BS - WS$$

Stratifications with larger BS - WS values provide greater variance reduction. The BS component measures systematic differences in prediction bias across strata, while the WS component (typically small under proportional allocation) reflects within-stratum residual heterogeneity.

See also

compute_variance_decomposition for the underlying decomposition.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Create candidate stratifications
candidates <- create_stratification_candidates(data, vars = c("Yhat", "word_count"))

# Compare using oracle decomposition
results <- compare_decomposition_oracle(data, candidates, n_code = 200)

# View summary table
results$summary
} # }
